blinding_guess.why: From what was read while describing, without further investigation: the GetParameters server callback (parameter_service.py:78-87) replaces response.values with an empty list as soon as any requested name is undeclared or uninitialized, whereas the GetParameters.srv response comment says 'values' is the same length and order as the names, with PARAMETER_NOT_SET for unset parameters (the snapshot's tests assert results.values == [] at test_parameter_client.py:191 and test_parameter_service.py:76). The ListParameters callback also matches separator-less names with name.startswith(prefix) (parameter_service.py:107-110), so a prefix such as 'param' would return both 'param_1' and 'param_2', and a name can be appended once per matching prefix. Either would be a defect in the listed elements.

notes: rclpy is the Python client library; it provides the per-node parameter services through ParameterService, created for every Node unless start_parameter_services=False. Service names are built as TOPIC_SEPARATOR_STRING.join((node.get_name(), 'get_parameters' | 'list_parameters')), i.e. the relative name '<node name>/get_parameters', expanded in the node's namespace; the 'param_demo' part of the packet names is the node name supplied at run time by the user of the library, not a literal in this snapshot. declares uses the packet names on that basis (they are what rclpy serves for a node named param_demo in the root namespace). msg_type is written pkg/Type; the code imports the types from rcl_interfaces.srv. The GetParameters/ListParameters definitions are not in the snapshot; they belong to the dependency rcl_interfaces and were fetched as raw .srv files at tag 1.6.0 (iron release line) and at branch iron (byte-identical). Hashes are the sha256_normalised proxy, not ROS 2 type hashes. msg and field ports carry definition_id but no QoS, since QoS belongs to the service endpoints. QoS: the code fixes qos_profile=qos_profile_parameters (rmw_qos_profile_parameters) for both services. The concrete policy values are defined in rmw/include/rmw/qos_profiles.h, outside the allowed sources; reliable/volatile are recorded from the snapshot's own documentation of that profile (qos.py:455 and 458-459: the services profile is reliable/volatile and the parameters profile is 'similar to service QoS profile but with larger queue depth'). Deadline is not set by the code; left null. Behaviour relevant to the field element: _get_parameters_callback appends one ParameterValue per requested name, but on ParameterNotDeclaredException or ParameterUninitializedException it sets response.values = node.get_parameters([]) (an empty list) and returns, discarding values already appended. _list_parameters_callback: for names without '.', when prefixes are given it appends the name once for every prefix the name startswith (no exact-match or separator check); for dotted names it requires startswith(prefix + '.') and filters by depth unless DEPTH_RECURSIVE (the constant request.DEPTH_RECURSIVE is referenced at line 117; not listed in references because it is a constant, not a field). param_1/param_2: rclpy does not declare them; parameter names are declared by user nodes at run time via Node.declare_parameter. Response fields written by rclpy other than GetParameters.values (ListParameters.result, ListParametersResult.names/prefixes) are not packet elements and are not listed.
